title: Introduce micro-load runners and dependency cleanup for perf pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our end-to-end perf and load test pipelines are slow, flaky, and expensive to run in CI. The current heavy-weight Python-based harness (long interpreter cold starts, large runtime deps, container build time) coupled with monolithic scenario runners increases CI runtime, causes noisy flaky failures, and makes iterating on perf tests slow.

Goal: Reduce CI runtime and flakiness for perf/eval pipelines, make test runners lightweight and easy to iterate locally, and remove/upgrade outdated dependencies that cause security/noise. Deliver a migration path that keeps historical eval comparability and integrates with existing dashboards and alerting.

Scope: Build and ship a small, single-purpose "micro-load runner" (Go binary) for the most common smoke/load scenarios; create an adapter layer so existing scenario specs (YAML) can run on either the legacy Python harness or the micro-runner; upgrade key Python and infra dependencies; shrink base container images; and add CI caching for compiled artifacts. This ticket covers the core refactor and dependency upgrades required for the migration (follow-ups will split out additional scenarios and full migration).
acceptance_criteria: New micro-load runner binary (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) built by CI and published as artifact
Adapter layer translates existing YAML scenario specs to micro-runner invocations without changing YAML schema
CI workflows using micro-runner reduce median pipeline runtime for perf smoke jobs by >=40% compared to baseline (measured across 10 runs)
Flaky failure rate for perf smoke CI jobs reduced by >=60% (baseline window: last 30 runs)
All upgraded dependencies listed in PR are security-reviewed and have release notes linked
Documentation updated: runbook for local dev, CI migration checklist, and dashboards annotated with new job IDs
No change to perf measurement semantics (token counts, latency measurement windows) — results must remain comparable to historical runs
At least one canary rollout of micro-runner in CI (small subset of perf jobs) completed and validated
migration_plan: Phase 0: Triage and baseline collection — capture current CI timings, flakiness metrics, and artifact sizes
Phase 1: Implement micro-runner MVP (minimal scenario features: single request, concurrency, simple KV caching toggle)
Phase 2: Adapter + spec translation tool that maps YAML->micro-runner flags; include validation step
Phase 3: Gradual CI rollout — add micro-runner as optional path for smoke perf jobs, run in parallel with legacy harness for 2 weeks
Phase 4: Cutover of low-risk smoke jobs, continue expanding scenario coverage; schedule follow-up tickets for complex scenarios
Phase 5: Finalize dependency upgrades for Python harness and remove deprecated libraries once all scenarios are ported
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter translation (cover 100% of flags used by smoke scenarios)
Integration test: micro-runner invoked from CI container, emits same measurement keys as legacy harness
Stability test: run micro-runner 500 iterations locally with varying concurrency and random seed to exercise corner cases
Benchmark test: run parallel comparison pipeline (legacy vs micro-runner) across 10 runs and publish comparison artifact to S3
Security scan: Snyk/OSV results for upgraded deps attached to PR
rollout: Stage 1 (Canary): Add micro-runner to smoke-perf-fast job and keep legacy harness enabled; run for 10 CI cycles and compare metrics
Stage 2: Flip default to micro-runner for smoke-perf-fast; keep legacy harness available under --legacy flag for 2 weeks
Stage 3: Replace legacy artifacts in CI Dockerfile and remove deprecated deps after no regressions for 2 weeks
Rollback plan: If perf delta >5% or flakiness increases, revert CI to legacy harness and open incident runbook
metrics: Artifact size reduction: base container image 1.8GB -> goal: <=800MB
Cost reduction estimate: ~35% cost savings for perf CI minute consumption
Measurement parity: mean latency difference between harnesses within +/-2% for smoke scenarios
notes: Rationale for Go micro-runner: compiled binary has much faster startup than Python + reduces image complexity; Go cross-compile makes multi-arch artifacts simple
We intentionally keep protocol surface minimal (stdin/out JSON events) so adapters can be rewritten in other languages if needed
Adapter will be a thin translator — not reimplementing full scenario language; complex scenario features (long stateful workflows, multi-step orchestrations) are out-of-scope for MVP
We will keep a compatibility layer to allow historical comparisons and retain legacy harness until parity is demonstrated
Potential follow-ups: translate remaining heavy scenarios, add OTLP metrics from micro-runner, and port key parts of observation stack to the runner
